Some friends of ours - named Dick and Jane for the purposes of this post - had been married for 33 years. They had two sons, both currently in their mid- to late-twenties.

Last April, they divorced. And boy was it messy. Without going into nasty detail, they both made it difficult on each other, and in the end, Dick signed an agreement to pay a certain amount of alimony to Jane each month, and even agreed to use said alimony to make her car payment, insurance payment, and mortgage payments for her. And he followed this agreement well.

Until now.

Suddenly, Dick decided that he didn't want to make Jane's car payments or insurance payments any longer. Perhaps he had come into hard times. Perhaps the devil was whispering in his ear. Whatever the cause, it is neither here nor there, at this point. Because Dick had hatched a plan.

As it happens, Jane's car was purchased under the name of their son (whom I will henceforth refer to as Dick Jr.). This was because neither Dick nor Jane had the sufficient credit at the time to purchase the car on their own. Meanwhile, Dick Jr. has been driving a beat-up old Honda which was under Jane's name.

Well, Dick reaches out to Dick Jr., and thus commences their plotting and scheming. Dick no longer wishes to honor his divorce agreement, in the form of making payments on the car and the car insurance (that these payments were being made by him out of the alimony that he agreed to pay Jane is overlooked). Dick and Dick Jr. decide that they are taking it upon themselves to improve their station in life, at the expense of Jane, who is none the wiser.

Under cover of darkness, Dick Jr. arrives at Jane's house. He finds her car - heretofore being paid for by Dick, using the alimony that he owes Jane - sitting in the driveway. Dick Jr. is somehow in possession of a key to the vehicle (I'm hazy on the details as to how he got said key). Dick Jr. writes Jane a note to the effect of "taking back my rightful property", and he proceeds to steal Jane's car. He leaves his Honda sitting in front of her house, gas tank empty and car battery dead.

Jane leaves her house the following morning, and to her great surprise, her car is missing! On her doorstep is the handwritten note from Dick Jr. Angry phone calls between family members and lawyers ensue. The police are unable to do anything, as the vehicle is technically in Dick Jr.'s name.

Two days later, Dick pays off the outstanding loan on Jane's car, allowing Dick Jr. to sell it. Dick Jr. then purchases a new vehicle with his ill-gotten earnings. Jane is left with the shitty old Honda. As the divorce agreement had specified that Dick was to pay insurance and loan installments on Jane's old car specifically, Dick now withholds that portion of alimony which he would have spent on that car, because Jane no longer has possession of it. Jane is then forced to change her insurance to cover the shitty Honda, and pay the insurance premium herself, as Dick is withholding part of the alimony.

Meanwhile, Jane consults her lawyer.

TL;DR - A married couple divorces. Ex-husband conspires with their son to steal ex-wife's car, to alleviate ex-husband's alimony payments, without breaking the law. Ex-wife is then stuck with shitty car that doesn't run.
